passage:
Dear Tarun,

I'm writing because I find it easier to say this without watching your face. You told me about the affair three weeks ago. Since then I've been angry every morning and hopeful every night, and I don't know which one is telling the truth. You say you want to rebuild, and part of me wants that too.

So here is what I need. Full honesty, including the answers I don't like. Time, without being asked how I'm doing every day. And your patience if I go cold.

I also want you to know that I might decide our marriage can't be saved. If I do, it won't mean I didn't love you or that I gave up too easily.

I'll give you my answer when I have one.

Nilesh

qa.q: How long ago did Tarun tell Nilesh about the affair?
What two feelings does Nilesh describe, and how does Nilesh feel about them?
qa.a: Anger every morning and hope every night. Nilesh does not know which one is telling the truth.

qa.q: What conditions does Nilesh set, and why are they reasonable?
qa.a: Full honesty, time without daily check-ins, and patience with coldness. They give Nilesh a way to judge whether trust can grow again without rushing.

qa.q: How might Tarun react on reading that Nilesh may decide the marriage cannot be saved?
qa.a: Tarun may feel afraid or sad, but the letter also says that choice would not mean Nilesh didn't love Tarun, which may make it easier to hear.

grounding: Shows a partner's hope tangled with anger after an affair, setting conditions of honesty and time, and stating that ending the marriage is a possible, legitimate choice.
